objective: Review the visual auto-repair instruction change for correctness and consistency with the rest of the root and specialist text.
scope: Diff: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/e4ac10e5-b710-572b-aa70-34045c8c8d11/scratchpad/visual-rules.diff (branch ccr-046ad103-6qsvgx-visual-autofix in /home/user/holyagent-visual; generated prompts in packages/integrations/claude/dist/agents). Intent: every visual finding with a legibility, overlap, responsiveness, accuracy, accessibility or interaction effect is repaired and re-inspected without asking, whatever severity the reviewer gave; only pure taste is skipped and named in the final report; the root never offers fixes it can make itself. Check contradictions with the assignments rule that only blocking findings start a repair, the Writing instructions rules, and size.

criteria.text: Findings are ranked blocking or non-blocking with file, line and fix, or their absence is stated

result:
result: The visual auto-repair change is consistent with the Assignments rule on blocking findings, but it leaves one blocking conflict with the decision rule and several non-blocking wording, size and ride-along issues.
changed: none (read-only review)
checks: none run. No shell, so `mise run verify` and `mise run build` were not run and the dist sync was checked by reading only. `git status` was not checked, so the worktree may differ from the diff file.
blockers:
1. [blocking] `/home/user/holyagent-visual/packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/visual.md:7` says "Repair material findings yourself and do not ask the user first" with no exception. `root/asking.md:3` and `requirements.md:14` (R-DECIDE) require every pending decision to go through AskUserQuestion, and `asking.md:3` covers anything that materially changes the result. A material finding whose only fix changes an explicit user requirement, or needs a choice between two fixes, has no route. Fix: scope the sentence to repairs that keep the user's requirements and need no choice, and route the rest through AskUserQuestion with a recommended default. Mirror the scope in `requirements.md:30` (R-VISUAL), which also says "without asking the user".
notes:
- `root/assignments.md:13` lets non-blocking findings "ride along" with a writer's repair, while `root/visual.md:5` says pure preference "stays unrepaired". Fix: exclude visual preference from ride-along, or change one of the two sentences.
- `root/visual.md:7` and `roles/worker-visual/purpose.md:1` say "repeat until the inspection is clean" with no round limit. A finding that cannot be cleared (blocked device, conflicting references) loops forever. Fix: after three failed rounds on one finding, stop and report it as a blocker, as `requirements.md:108` (R-WD) already does for debugging.
- Size and duplication: the Assignment names no expected size, so the size check has no target. Measured by word count, the Judging section in `visual.md` grew from about 90 to about 190 words, and R-VISUAL from about 80 to about 115. The "material" definition now appears in `visual.md:5`, `requirements.md:30`, `interface-inspection.md:7` (generated into dist `worker-visual.md:176` and `reviewer-visual.md:143`), `assignments.md:13`, the two purposes and `reviewer-visual/frontend-design.md:3`. R-INSPECT requires the fixed copies in the specialist roles. Fix: make `assignments.md:13` point to "Judging visual work" and cut the purpose lines to a pointer.
- Wording drift for the same rule: `requirements.md:30` says "the accuracy of its text and numbers" where `visual.md:5` and `interface-inspection.md:7` say "whether the text and numbers state the content correctly". The viewport scope is worded three ways ("the criteria list", "listed", "listed"). The severity/size wording also differs ("whatever severity", "of any size"). `reviewer-visual/frontend-design.md:3` lists the effects without acceptance, interaction correctness, composition or text accuracy. Fix: use the `visual.md:5` wording everywhere, and in `frontend-design.md:3` point to the interface inspection list instead of repeating it.
- Obsolete phrase: `roles/worker-visual/purpose.md:1` (dist `worker-visual.md:4` and `:15`) says "including those a reviewer listed as small". Reviewers now mark every material finding blocking, so the phrase is redundant. Fix: delete it.
- `specialist/merge-ready.md:9` lists "Edge polish nobody asked for" as the non-blocking behavior case, and the worker's rubric has no visual row. A worker could file a small legibility defect as polish. Fix: add a visual row saying a material discrepancy under interface inspection is blocking.
- `root/visual.md:7` "Name any preference you skipped in the final report as a statement" is vague. Fix: "name each skipped preference in the final report, without a fix".
- Checked and consistent: the requirements file changed before the instruction sets, as `holyagent.md` "Writing instructions" asks. The dist text matches the source for `holyagent.md:75` and `:87`, `worker-visual.md:4` and `:15`, and `reviewer-visual.md:15` and `:143`. The diff adds no capital-letter emphasis.
evidence:
Findings are ranked blocking or non-blocking with file, line and fix, or their absence is stated: met. The blocking finding and the non-blocking notes above each give file, line and fix.
